text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Necessary amendments to the electoral law are likely to be made that will require all candidates to declare that they were not tax defaulters, caretaker prime minister Meraj Khalid said.
- Asif Zardari, the detained husband of Benazir Bhutto, has been shifted to Karachi from Islamabad.
- The government has decided to merge the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan, Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan and the Cotton Export Corporation into one organisation.
- Spinners are planning to form a cooperative society with a mandate to maintain a buffer stock of raw materials like cotton and synthetic fibres for the industry.
- A high level official delegation, led by economic advisor Shahid Javed Burki, would visit Japan early December to explore possibilities of floating yen-denominated Samurai bonds.
- The state-owned banks and financial institutions would be issued 20-year maturity bonds bearing a return of 13 percent a year against their non-performing loans, sources said.
- Gold imports rose to 2.5 tonnes in November from 1.3 tonnes in September, officials said.
- A report on tariff reforms is being finalised and its contents will be made public by early December, Commerce Minister Muhammad Zubair Khan said.
- The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association has asked the State (central) Bank of Pakistan for credit facility of about 53 billion rupees needed as working capital for the next six months.
- The state-run United Bank Limited would be privatised through open bidding, Salman Shah, chairman of the state's Privatisation Commission said.
- Delay in issuance of a quality certificate could hurt potential export orders of 900,000 tonnes of rice to the European Union, sources said.
